# sigv4 — AWS Signature Version 4 happy path.
# Boots the sigv4 scenario, runs one drain, and asserts the events JSONL
# and redacted trace JSONL match the golden. The server re-derives the
# SigV4 signature from the received request and compares it to the wire
# Authorization header, so a 200 + events proves the client signed
# correctly. The spec is loaded live from the embedded template.
#
# The signature is computed with real wall-clock time (never the pinned
# SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH clock), so Authorization and X-Amz-Date are
# non-deterministic on the wire — the trace golden is stable only because
# both headers are redacted.

exec skopos template show -o spec.yml sigv4
replace spec.yml http://localhost:9999 $URL
exec skopos run -i spec.yml --once --trace trace.jsonl --out events.jsonl
normalize trace.jsonl
cmp trace.jsonl want_trace.jsonl
cmp events.jsonl want_events.jsonl

-- want_trace.jsonl --
{"elapsed":"<scrubbed>","iteration":1,"method":"GET","query":{"limit":"<ref state.page_size>","since":"<ref state.last_timestamp>"},"request_headers":{"Accept":"application/json, application/x-ndjson;q=0.9, */*;q=0.1","Authorization":"<redacted>","X-Amz-Date":"<redacted>"},"response_body":"body 348 bytes, object-like","started_at":"<scrubbed>","status":200,"url":"$URL_HOST/sigv4/events"}
-- want_events.jsonl --
{"id":"evt-000001","seq_num":1,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}
{"id":"evt-000002","seq_num":2,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:01Z"}
{"id":"evt-000003","seq_num":3,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:02Z"}
{"id":"evt-000004","seq_num":4,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:03Z"}
{"id":"evt-000005","seq_num":5,"timestamp":"2026-01-01T00:00:04Z"}
